before.when: Wisconsin exemptions are allowable, the asset is a motor vehicle, and the case has one debtor.
before.procedure: Include Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g). Its ceiling is $4,000 plus any unused amount of the $12,000 consumer-goods exemption in paragraph (d). Because EV evaluates each asset-exemption pair independently without allocating an aggregate across other assets, use a $16,000 ceiling when the facts do not establish another use of paragraph (d), then report the lesser of the vehicle's whole value and that ceiling.
before.avoid_when: Do not blindly report $4,000 when the paragraph (d) amount is unused, report more than the vehicle's value, apply the motor-vehicle provision to nonvehicles, or infer a married-couple ceiling from this one-debtor rule.

after.when: Wisconsin exemptions are allowable, the asset is a motor vehicle, and the case has one debtor.
after.procedure:
For each vehicle independently, include Wis. Stat. § 815.18(3)(g) and calculate its whole-asset claim in three steps: treat the $12,000 paragraph (d) capacity as unused unless the facts expressly establish another use; add it to the $4,000 motor-vehicle amount to obtain a $16,000 ceiling; then report the lesser of the vehicle's value and $16,000.
Execution example: A hypothetical vehicle worth $10,000 receives a § 815.18(3)(g) claim of $10,000; one worth $25,000 receives $16,000.
after.avoid_when: Do not stop at $4,000 when paragraph (d) capacity is unused, reduce that capacity by independently evaluated assets, exceed the vehicle's value, apply the provision to a nonvehicle, or infer a married-couple ceiling from this one-debtor rule.
